review_kind.correlation: Same agent team/model workflow as source authors. This is a bounded assumption/source/control review, not an independent mathematical or native-kernel validation.

actual_source_review.generic_contract: For an arbitrary binary relation R on Node and a map address : Node -> List Label, preservation is forall a b, R a b -> IsPrefix (address a) (address b); reflection is the reverse implication. If R a c and R b c, both assumptions force R a b or R b a. If neither comparison holds, no map satisfying both exists.
actual_source_review.proof_boundary: The actual comparable_of_common_upper proof applies List.prefix_or_prefix_of_prefix to the two preserved comparisons, then reflection to both branches. The obstruction consumes explicit hac, hbc, not-hab and not-hba. It requires no order axioms, injectivity, source finiteness or inhabited/finite target alphabet. No converse representation theorem is stated.
actual_source_review.actual_chain: chainAddress n is List.replicate n (). Actual prefix iff m <= n is proved using the upstream replicate theorem; preservation/reflection and injectivity are separate proved consumers.
actual_source_review.actual_diamond: The four-constructor Diamond has relation a = bottom OR b = top OR a = b, with reflexivity, transitivity and antisymmetry proved in the library. left and right are incomparable and each is below top. The actual obstruction theorem quantifies over any Label type.
actual_source_review.same_map_counterexample: diamondRank sends bottom,left,right,top to 0,1,2,3; diamondAddress is the corresponding Unit-list length. The same map is proved injective and preserving, while address left is a prefix of address right and DiamondLe left right is false. Thus injective preservation alone does not discharge reflection.
actual_source_review.positive_control: Actual final positive file consumes the generic obstruction, exact chain prefix equivalence, concrete diamond obstruction, same-map injectivity/preservation/reflection failure, an actual false source comparison and both actual common-upper comparisons. The three order-law proofs are present in the library; the positive file does not separately invoke each law.
actual_source_review.negative_control: Actual final negative file asks for ReflectsPrefix DiamondLe diamondAddress and supplies diamondAddress_preserves. It is precisely a preservation-versus-reflection mismatch for the concrete map, not a generic placeholder hypothesis.
actual_source_review.findings: No actionable omitted hypothesis or false preservation/reflection inference observed in the bounded final-source read.

sources.title: Semilinear metric semilattices on R-trees
locations: Section 3, Definition 1 and semilinearity definition, PDF page 4
Theorem 1 and its rooted-order construction, PDF pages 1 and 4-5
sources.correspondence: Section 3 defines lower semilinearity by linearly ordered lower cones, matching the necessary cone property obtained locally. The paper constructs the reverse ancestor orientation as an upper-semilinear order on a rooted R-tree.
sources.limits: Its R-tree criterion also needs a geodesic metric space and compatible semilattice distance identities. It is not a finite-list representation theorem. Reversing the order changes which cones are linear; these directions cannot be interchanged silently. Only the order terminology and orientation comparison are used.

sources.title: Incomparable copies of a poset in the Boolean lattice
sources.correspondence: The opening definitions distinguish an injective strict-order-preserving map into the Boolean lattice from an induced embedding that also reflects strict order. This supports keeping preservation, injectivity and reflection distinct in the review.
sources.limits: The target is a Boolean lattice and the source convention uses strict order. The local theorem uses an arbitrary binary relation and non-strict List.IsPrefix. No direct formal translation or proof port from this paper is claimed; the local prefix obstruction follows the pinned Lean list theorem.

primary_arxiv_scout.novelty: The local theorem is a direct reusable consequence of the existing ancestor-comparability API with explicit relation-preserving/reflection premises. Neither cited paper is asserted to contain the exact local Lean theorem.

findings.finding: The order quantity counts choices of leaves in a 3SUM tensor construction; order_nonneg assumes contribution and the output inner-set cardinality, and order_le bounds this integer quantity. The file name does not establish a poset-order or reflection result.
